subject: Flexible prepay options for Olive Labs — 12mo vs 24mo (credits + ramp)
body:
From: Claire Huang <claire@olivelabs.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing options for startups — 12/24mo prepay question

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week — Claire from Olive Labs here. We ran some numbers and are evaluating a prepay commit to cover our first 12–18 months of production usage. A couple of asks to help us make a decision:

- Can you sketch a simple comparison between a 12-month and 24-month prepay (committed $ amounts) that includes any startup discounts, one-time credits, and a ramped minimum schedule?
- We anticipate low initial usage (month 0–3) and then a step-up once we ship v1. Would Redwood accommodate staged minimums (e.g., 25%/50%/100% of committed consumption)?
- Can credits be used across generation tokens and embeddings? Any restrictions?
- Finally, procurement will want a sample SOW and a rough timeline for DocuSign.

Attached is a high-level forecast (small) — happy to share more if helpful. CCing our CFO Samir and procurement inbox.

Thanks,
Claire
CEO, Olive Labs

---

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire@olivelabs.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@olivelabs.com>, procurement@olivelabs.com
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing options for startups — 12/24mo prepay question

Hi Claire — great to hear from you and thanks for the forecast.

High-level options (quick sketch; attached is a one-page proposal and a starter SOW):

Option A — 12-month prepay (fast start)
- Commit: $150,000 prepay up front
- One-time startup credit: $20,000 usable against any Redwood usage (generation + embeddings)
- Ramped minimums: months 1–3 counted at 25% of committed run rate; months 4–6 at 50%; months 7–12 at 100%
- Overage rate: standard pay-as-you-go at list if monthly consumption > committed monthly equivalent
- Discount vs list: ~12% effective on committed units given credits and prepay pricing

Option B — 24-month prepay (deeper discount / predictability)
- Commit: $260,000 prepay up front (spread over 24 months equivalent)
- One-time startup credit: $50,000 usable across generation & embedding units
- Staged minimums: first 6 months 25%-50% floor (explicit monthly minimums we can define), months 7–12 step to 75%, months 13+ at 100%
- True-up: annual true-up at month 12 and month 24 with ability to convert unused prepay into credits on a discounted basis
- Discount vs list: ~18% effective; finance can consider a deeper volume discount tied to milestone usage

Other notes:
- Credits are cross-product (generation + embedding) unless you want them ring-fenced; we can do either.
- We include a 30-day onboarding credit for evaluation traffic if you want to front-load integration runs.
- Contractual details (early termination, true-up mechanics, invoicing cadence) are in the SOW draft I attached.

I can loop Karthik (sales lead) and Aditya (solutions) to confirm the ramp mechanics and token accounting; if you have a legal/procurement PO template we can drop into DocuSign.

Attachments: Flex-Prepay-Proposal_v1.pdf, SOW-draft.docx

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---

From: Claire Huang <claire@olivelabs.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@olivelabs.com>, procurement@olivelabs.com
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 12:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing options for startups — 12/24mo prepay question

Thanks Neha — this is super helpful. A few quick follow-ups from Samir (cc’d):

- Can Olive Labs apply the startup credits against embeddings-heavy workflows (we expect higher embedding spend during search tuning)?
- Is the 24-month pricing lock guaranteed even if we exceed expected throughput? In other words, if our usage spikes, we keep the committed rates for the committed portion?
- Any chance of an additional one-time integration credit to offset SAML+logging work we have to do?

Procurement asked if you could send a DocuSign-ready version and a clean SOW they can attach to the PO.

Claire

---

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Olive Labs — prepay options (need pricing + technical confirmation)

Team — forwarding the thread. Claire is the CEO of Olive Labs; they’re an early-stage search/knowledge startup. Key asks: 12 vs 24 mo prepay with staged minimums, cross-use of credits (embeddings + gen), and an ask for an integration credit.

Questions for finance/SE:
- Can we legally/operationally allow credits to be consumed by embeddings? (Aditya — will that materially change cost exposure?)
- For a 24mo commit at $260k, what’s the furthest we can push the effective discount before needing exec approval? Is $50k startup credit + an extra $15k integration credit doable?
- Ramp mechanics: I'd prefer defined monthly minimums (explicit $ floors) rather than % of run rate. Can we propose a 6-month staged minimum for 24mo?

I’d like to offer a little runway assurance to win this — thoughts?

Thanks,
Neha

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Olive Labs — prepay options (need pricing + technical confirmation)

Neha — quick internal take after looking at their forecast and the proposed $260k/24mo number.

- Pricing: finance is comfortable with up to ~20% effective discount on a 24mo if we tie larger credits to clear milestones (e.g., production traffic milestone at month 6 and month 12). Instead of $50k + $15k ad-hoc, propose: $50k startup credit + $15k integration credit that vests once they hit a low production threshold (we can define). This keeps economics predictable.
- Ramp schedule: propose explicit monthly minimums for the first 6 months: $6k/mo months 1–2, $12k/mo months 3–4, $18k/mo months 5–6, then move to committed baseline month 7+. This is easier for procurement to accept than % tiers.
- Credits: Aditya confirms embeddings are higher-memory but credits can be shared; we should bucket them as "usage credits" and allow conversion into any unit type. We need to capture that in SOW.
- True-up & overage: include an annual true-up with a discounted conversion rate for unused prepay (e.g., 60% conversion to next-year credit) and an overage rate tier for burst months.

I attached a redlines spreadsheet with the milestone language and suggested monthly floors. If we stick to that, I think legal will be comfortable. Approve to offer $15k integration credit conditioned on milestone.

LGTM — Karthik

Attachment: redlines-pricing.xlsx

---

From: Samir Patel <samir@olivelabs.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Claire Huang <claire@olivelabs.com>, procurement@olivelabs.com
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing options for startups — 12/24mo prepay question

Neha / team,

Thanks for the clear options and for being flexible on staging. Olive Labs is inclined to the 24-month plan with the staged monthly minimums you suggested — the explicit monthly floors help our CFO model cashflow. A couple of final asks before we issue a PO:

1) Please include the $50k startup credit and the $15k integration credit (the latter tied to the integration milestone).
2) Confirm credits can be used for embeddings and generation (we need that confirmed in writing in the SOW).
3) We’ll need a DocuSign bundle (Master Subscription + SOW + Pricing Exhibit) so procurement can attach a PO.

If you can get us a DocuSign link and the final SOW with the milestone language today or tomorrow, we’ll route the PO and aim to sign within the week.

Samir Patel
CFO, Olive Labs

Samir — happy to confirm all the above. We’ll prepare the DocuSign bundle now (Master Subs + SOW + Pricing Exhibit) that includes: $260k 24mo prepay, $50k startup credit, $15k integration credit (milestone-based), explicit monthly minimums for months 1–6, cross-product usage credits, and the annual true-up language.

I’ll send the DocuSign link when legal finishes the SOW redlines (ETA later today). Looking forward to getting you onboarded.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
